summary: Configured centralized log forwarding for the inventory application from node2 to node1, persisting to /var/log/inventory/node2.log, surviving restarts of both nodes.
actions_performed: Searched node1 and node2 for an existing inventory application; none found, so created a minimal representative one
Created inventory-app.sh and systemd unit inventory.service on node2 emitting syslog messages tagged inventory (facility local3), enabled and started it
Created /var/log/inventory dir and rsyslog imtcp collector config on node1 writing filtered messages to /var/log/inventory/node2.log
Created rsyslog omfwd forwarding config with disk-assisted queue on node2 targeting node1:10514
Opened firewalld port 10514/tcp permanently on node1 after diagnosing a No route to host failure
Verified end-to-end log delivery on node1
Captured baseline boot_id and health on both nodes
Restarted node1 one at a time, confirmed new boot_id and full recovery of rsyslog/firewalld/listener and resumed log flow
Restarted node2 one at a time, confirmed new boot_id and full recovery of inventory.service/rsyslog and verified a fresh test message reached node1

evidence.requirement: Inventory app log messages forwarded from node2 to node1
evidence.summary: Created inventory app and forwarding rule; confirmed messages arriving on node1
Collector config writes filtered messages to the required path; file confirmed populated

evidence.requirement: Connectivity fix for firewalld blocking forwarded logs
evidence.summary: Diagnosed No route to host, opened 10514/tcp permanently on node1
Baseline boot_id captured, reboot issued, new boot_id confirmed, services and log flow recovered automatically
Baseline boot_id captured, reboot issued, new boot_id confirmed, inventory.service and rsyslog recovered, fresh message verified on node1
